explanation: South West Growth Area. ABS ranks Austral-Greendale among NSW's fastest-growing areas (+16% in 2023-24). The +1,908 bonds fit large house-and-land and granny-flat build-out.
Huntlee new town at North Rothbury is still releasing stages (Stage 7A town centre). A small 2021 base of 654 bonds makes +576 bonds plausible.

place: Box Hill, Marsden Park, Riverstone, Vineyard
explanation: North West Growth Area. ABS: Box Hill-Nelson added 4,042 people and Marsden Park-Shanes Park 3,500 in 2023-24 alone. This easily explains +2,283 bonds.
Wollondilly fringe growth: 842 residential approvals in five years, and population rose from 5,777 (2021) to 8,611 (2025). Estates include Myrtle Estate and The Gardens. +365 bonds fits.

Not a lockdown rebound: neighbours 2010 (-2%) and 2015 (0%) didn't rebound. New student housing that lodges per-bed bonds drives it: Scape Redfern (534 beds, 2021) and Y Suites on Regent (408 beds, 2024).
North West Growth Area around Tallawong Metro. ABS: Schofields-East added about 2,700 people in 2023-24, so the +1,242 bonds reflect real new homes.

category: Lockdown or border rebound (students, CBD renters away in 2021)
explanation: Students returning after borders reopened. The +1,075 bonds exceed the 366 extra empty homes and the neighbours' rebound (2008 +17%, 2009 -4%). Refilled student-housing beds that carry bonds probably fill the gap.
Watagan Park (Johnson Property Group, 2,500 lots planned) is still registering lots and completing homes into 2025-26. +205 bonds on a small base is plausible.
Frasers' Ed.Square (about 1,884 apartments and terraces) has delivered stages from 2020 to 2025 next to the station. This plausibly explains +494 bonds.

place: Gillieston Heights, Lochinvar, Heddon Greta, Cliftleigh, Morpeth, Hinton
explanation: Maitland fringe urban release areas: Lochinvar (about 5,000 homesites planned, 650 lots at Lochinvar Ridge) and Gillieston Heights (330-lot subdivision). This fits +735 bonds.

Small infill subdivisions around Thirlmere (Eden Rise, about 15 lots; Marion St and Morris Cres releases). Dwellings rose 1,608 to 2,107 from 2016 to 2021. Small base (+146 bonds) and not robust across variants.

Ongoing apartment boom: dwellings rose 9,347 to 12,117 (2016-21). Lidcombe Rise (376 units, late 2023) added 220 market, 93 affordable and 63 social homes. The 2021 vacancy of 9.3% (5.4% in 2016) points to some lockdown or lease-up rebound too.

place: Gregory Hills, Gledswood Hills, Catherine Field, Rossmore
explanation: South West Growth Area estates. Dwellings more than doubled, 2,809 to 6,424 (2016-21), and new homes are still being listed in Gregory Hills and Catherine Field in 2026. The +524 bond rise is real new stock.

place: Picton, Wilton, Buxton, Couridjah, Razorback, Maldon, Mowbray Park
explanation: Wilton Growth Area: Bingara Gorge plus Wilton Greens, where civil works on the first 263 lots began in March 2021 (up to 3,600 homes planned), and North Wilton, where homes are under construction. Dwellings rose 4,120 to 4,638 (2016-21).

place: Thornton, Chisholm, Beresfield, Woodberry, Tarro, Black Hill, Hexham
explanation: Chisholm release area: AVID's Waterford grew from 750 to 1,700 blocks after 2017, had more than 4,000 residents by 2023, and is due to finish in 2028. Dwellings rose 7,279 to 9,325 (2016-21).

place: Eastgardens, Hillsdale, Matraville, Malabar, Chifley, Little Bay, La Perouse, Phillip Bay, Port Botany
explanation: Meriton's Pagewood Green at Eastgardens: Pagewood Centro Uccello (375 build-to-rent units, completed 2024) and the build-to-rent Marigold (about 127 units). The 2021 vacancy of 8.6% also suggests lockdown and lease-up rebound. New units explain about half of the +1,056 bonds.

place: Cessnock, Bellbird, Bellbird Heights, Nulkaba, Aberdare, Abernethy, Kearsley
explanation: Dwellings rose only 8% (11,706 to 12,661) over 2016-21. Some new Bellbird estates exist (Mount View Grange, North Ridge), but they can't explain a 24% bond rise. Investor purchases, owner homes turned rentals, or granny flats are likely but unproven.

Showground Metro precinct apartments came after the Census: Chateau Showground (296 units, 2023), Hills Showground Village (430 units, staged to 2025) and Chapman Gardens (258 units, due 2024). Dwellings grew only 4.5% from 2016 to 2021.

category: Lockdown or border rebound (students, CBD renters away in 2021)
explanation: UNSW student area. In 2021 the population fell (16,689 to 14,643), vacancy jumped from 5.3% to 9.6%, and renters fell from 3,280 to 2,978. The Dec 2021 base came before students returned. Little new supply (Botanica, 58 units, 2025).

place: Camden, Oran Park, Cobbitty, Harrington Park, Spring Farm, Elderslie, Camden South
explanation: South West Growth Area. Dwellings rose 13,986 to 21,760 (2016-21). Oran Park Town kept releasing stages (Tranche 28 in 2025), and Mirvac's Cobbitty estate (900 homes, site bought 2021) is building out. The +1,101 bond rise is real new stock.

place: Jimboomba, Flagstone, Glenlogan, Riverbend, North Maclean, South Maclean, Stockleigh
explanation: Core of Greater Flagstone (about 50,000 homes planned; Flagstone, Glenlogan, Riverbend are in 4280). 2021 dwellings 6,886. Bonds +1,291 fits steady estate build-out.

place: Palmview, Mooloolah Valley, Mooloolah, Glenview, Diamond Valley
explanation: AVID's Harmony at Palmview (4,800 dwellings planned, still building). 2021 had 3,824 dwellings and 614 rented homes. Bonds +665 fits continued estate build-out.

place: Park Ridge, Park Ridge South, Munruben
explanation: Park Ridge masterplan estates. ABS: Boronia Heights - Park Ridge SA2 was one of Queensland's three largest growers in 2022-23 (+2,000 people). 2021 had 4,893 dwellings, 37% rented.

place: Ripley, South Ripley, Deebing Heights, Karalee, Fernvale, Mount Crosby, Walloon and rural Ipswich localities
explanation: Ripley Valley PDA (Ecco Ripley and others). Ripley SA2 grew about 2,000 people in 2022-23 and 2,703 in 2023-24, Queensland's largest. Bonds +2,836 fits that pace.

place: Greenbank, Silverbark Ridge, New Beith, Boronia Heights, Lyons
explanation: Mirvac's Everleigh in Greenbank (launched 2018; 869 homes built and 107 underway by 2025). Silverbark Ridge (Greater Flagstone) is in 4124. Greenbank - North Maclean SA2 grew 13% in 2022-23.

place: Logan Reserve, Chambers Flat, Waterford, Waterford West
explanation: Chambers Flat - Logan Reserve was Queensland's fastest-growing SA2 in 2022-23 (18.4%) and 2023-24 (19.1%, +2,419 people). AVID's Killara (about 749 homes) and Chambers Ridge (300) estates. Bonds +2,304 fits.

place: Acacia Ridge, Heathwood, Larapinta, Pallara, Willawong
explanation: Pallara - Willawong SA2 grew 14% in 2022-23, Queensland's second fastest, so building continued after 2021. Stockland Pallara (about 720 homes) plus many smaller Pallara and Heathwood estates.

place: Burrum Heads, Howard, Burrum Town, Burrum River, Pacific Haven, Beelbi Creek, Burgowan
explanation: Small coastal retiree area (median age 60) with 371 unoccupied, likely holiday, homes in 2021. +162 bonds on a 329 base probably mixes holiday homes turned rentals with some Dolphin Waters building. Not robust across variants.

Existing North Harbour estate (about 3,000 residents by 2025), townhouse projects (for example 64 homes at 11-15 Joyce St, done in 2023) and Sage Burpengary (homes from 2024). The 3,700-home North Harbour PDA only started in 2025.

Fairland's Summerstone (about 1,000 homes) and Ausbuild's Montrose (about 600 lots), plus smaller estates. Stockland Kinma Valley's first residents only moved in Oct 2025. 2021 base was already 43% rented.
Dwellings flat (1,946 to 1,965, 2016-21). No sizeable post-2021 project found; Wilga St Wacol complex dates from 2012. +207 bonds likely owner-to-rental conversion or a data issue.
Rochedale Urban Community greenfield area kept delivering homes. Dwellings rose 7,026 to 8,333 (2016-21); state funding in 2025 targets about 1,285 more homes.

category: Lockdown or border rebound (students, CBD renters away in 2021)
explanation: Mainly international student return after borders reopened: big student towers (Scape, UniLodge, about 1,200 beds, 2019-20) were half-empty in June 2021. Few new rental apartments since 2021.
Small townhouse and house-and-land infill (Northrise, 26 townhouses; Gumwood, Hamlyn Grove lots). Renters rose 790 to 947 (2016-21). No large estate, so steady growth.

category: Lockdown or border rebound (students, CBD renters away in 2021)
explanation: Mostly student return: UniLodge Park Central (1,578 beds, 2019) was short of foreign students in June 2021. New apartments since 2021 add only about 290 units.

place: Caloundra, Caloundra West, Pelican Waters, Golden Beach, Currimundi, Aura (Baringa, Nirimba, Banya, Bells Creek)
explanation: Stockland's Aura (Caloundra South) is in this postcode: about 2,700 homes by March 2022, with 800 more under way. Postcode dwellings rose 26,573 to 31,107 from 2016 to 2021.
Townhouse and small unit infill. Flats 0 to 40, townhouses 45 to 122, dwellings 2,213 to 2,467 (2016-21). Modest growth; 2021-26 projects not verified.
Hope Island apartment completions: Anchorage (230, 2022) and Athena Residences (185, 2023), plus Serenity villas. Dwellings 11,725 to 13,624 (2016-21). Fits +559 bonds.
Slow infill: dwellings 2,462 to 2,630 (2016-21) and small estates (Harvest 30, Carseldine Close 44). No large estate. 18% over 5.25 years is mild.
Moreton Bay greenfield: Narangba Heights (about 1,200 dwellings, still delivering) and Amity. 1,225 new addresses since 2021 in Narangba. Estates mostly owner-occupied, so +278 bonds fits.
